items.name: ai-chat
items.displayName: AI Chat (Azure OpenAI + App Service + Cosmos DB)
items.description: A chat API on App Service that calls an Azure OpenAI gpt-5-mini deployment and persists conversations in serverless Cosmos DB. All access is keyless via managed identity.

potentialUseCases: A customer-support or internal helpdesk chatbot
A product/document Q&A assistant (extend with retrieval from the AI landing zone)

items.name: event-streaming-analytics
items.description: Event Hubs ingestion, a Stream Analytics job shaping events to a curated lake, a Functions hot-path consumer, and Cosmos DB serving - all keyless.
items.what: Devices and apps publish to an Event Hubs namespace. A Stream Analytics job reads one consumer group, applies a windowed transformation, and lands curated Parquet in an ADLS-style container. An isolated-worker Functions app reads a second consumer group for the low-latency hot path and writes to a serverless Cosmos DB serving store. Event Hubs, Stream Analytics, and Functions all authenticate with managed identity (local auth disabled).
items.why: Telemetry, clickstream, and IoT scenarios need both a cheap durable cold path and a low-latency hot path off the same ingestion stream. This separates concerns with managed services so there are no Kafka clusters or polling jobs to operate, and no SAS keys to rotate.

Clickstream and product analytics pipeline
Fraud / anomaly hot path with a durable replay log
Operational metrics fan-out to a serving store and a lake

items.why: Microservices teams want async messaging, durable state, and event-driven autoscaling without running Kubernetes or managing broker credentials. Container Apps + Dapr provides the building-block APIs while Service Bus and Cosmos supply the backbone - and managed identity removes every connection string.
potentialUseCases: Order processing / saga workflows with a worker pool
Decoupled command and event services behind a single gateway
Burst-scaling background processing off a queue
Polyglot microservices needing portable state and pub/sub

items.name: multiregion-web
items.description: Azure Front Door Premium + WAF routing to App Service backends in two regions, backed by multi-region Cosmos DB with automatic failover.
items.what: A global Front Door profile with a managed WAF fronts two regional App Service deployments. Front Door health-probes both origins and load-balances across them; each web app accepts traffic only from Front Door (service tag + x-azure-fdid header). Cosmos DB replicates across both regions with automatic failover, optionally with multi-region writes.
items.why: Business-critical web workloads need to survive a regional outage and serve users with low latency worldwide. This template delivers an active-active footprint with a single global anycast entry point, automated failover, and origin lockdown - the standard mission-critical web pattern.
potentialUseCases: Mission-critical customer portal with an availability SLO
Global e-commerce storefront needing low latency per geography
Regulated workload requiring regional resilience and DR
Public API needing global WAF and DDoS protection

items.name: secure-web-app

items.description: Network-hardened App Service with private SQL and Key Vault behind private endpoints, fronted by Application Gateway with WAF.
items.what: A Linux App Service integrated into a VNet, talking to Azure SQL and Key Vault exclusively over private endpoints with private DNS. The only public ingress is an Application Gateway running an OWASP WAF policy in Prevention mode. Connectivity to SQL is passwordless via managed identity.
items.why: Most regulated web workloads cannot expose data services to the public internet or accept unfiltered inbound traffic. This baseline closes both gaps while keeping a passwordless, observable, zone-redundant footprint.

items.name: sql-data-api

items.description: A .NET API on App Service backed by Azure SQL Database, using passwordless managed-identity auth and Entra-only SQL administration. Dev runs serverless SQL; prod runs zone-redundant compute and database.
items.what: A .NET API on App Service backed by Azure SQL Database. The app authenticates to SQL passwordlessly via its managed identity, and the SQL server uses Microsoft Entra-only authentication. Dev uses serverless auto-pause SQL; prod uses zone-redundant compute and database.
items.why: Most business apps are a stateless API in front of a relational database. Doing it passwordlessly (managed identity + Entra-only SQL) removes the most common security failure - leaked connection strings - while the dev/prod split keeps lab costs low and production resilient.
